payload.rationale: I estimate a 60% chance that the Fed leaves rates unchanged at the October 28, 2026 meeting. This is a broad judgment based on general monetary-policy behavior, not an assessment informed by current economic releases or Fed communications. Policy rates often remain unchanged between meetings, and changing them typically requires sufficient evidence to support further tightening or easing. However, consecutive changes are common during active policy cycles, so persistence is only a weak guide without knowing the current regime. The estimate could be too high if the Fed is already pursuing consecutive cuts, or if incoming inflation or employment data strongly favor a change. It could be too low if policy is firmly on hold or policymakers want more time to assess earlier adjustments. Under the supplied settlement rule, cancellation of the scheduled meeting also qualifies as YES; I treat that as a minor possibility rather than a meaningful driver.
limitations: No current research or observations were supplied, and no browsing was available.
The September 2026 policy decision, prevailing target range, economic releases, and recent Fed guidance are not established by the supplied evidence.
The estimate relies on general policy behavior and has substantial uncertainty about the current policy regime.
Only information available by the specified September 18, 2026 cutoff is eligible; no later developments are assumed.
